introduction: Tailored for advanced legal exams and UPSC Civil Services, this level explores the historic implementation of the first state-level Uniform Civil Code in post-independence India (Uttarakhand UCC 2024), examining its radical provisions on live-in relationships and gender parity.

core_concepts.title: The Uttarakhand Uniform Civil Code, 2024
core_concepts.description:
Passed in February 2024, Uttarakhand became the first state in India to enact a UCC (Goa has a Portuguese-era civil code, but UK's is the first post-independence code).
- Applicability: Applies to all residents of Uttarakhand (irrespective of religion) AND to residents living outside the state. 
- Exclusions: It explicitly EXCLUDES Scheduled Tribes (STs) protected under Article 366(25) of the Constitution.

core_concepts.title: Radical Shifts in the Uttarakhand UCC
core_concepts.description:
1. Live-in Relationships: It legally mandates the **compulsory registration** of all live-in relationships within 1 month. Failure to register attracts criminal penalties (imprisonment up to 3 months/fine). Children born of registered live-in relationships are legally legitimate.
2. Ban on Bigamy/Polygamy: It absolutely prohibits polygamy across all religions within the state.
3. Ban on Halala and Iddat Restrictions: It criminalizes practices like Nikah Halala and removes any condition that prohibits a woman from remarrying immediately after a divorce.

core_concepts.title: Succession Parity in Uttarakhand UCC
core_concepts.description:
The UK UCC abolishes the discriminatory inheritance practices found in various personal laws.
- Equal Property Rights: It mandates absolute equality between sons and daughters in inheriting ancestral property, eradicating the remaining gender disparities in uncodified Muslim law and specific Hindu provisions.
- Parents as Class I Heirs: Both the mother *and* the father are elevated to Class I heirs (unlike the Hindu Succession Act where the father is Class II).

core_concepts.title: State Power to Enact a UCC (Article 44 vs Concurrent List)
core_concepts.description:
Can a State enact a UCC, or is it solely the Union's power?
- Constitutional Justification: 'Personal Law' (marriage, divorce, inheritance) falls under **Entry 5 of the Concurrent List** (List III) of the Seventh Schedule. Therefore, a State Legislature has the constitutional competence to pass laws overriding religious personal laws, provided it receives the President's assent (Article 254(2)) to resolve repugnancy with central laws.

important_entities.name: John Vallamattom v. Union of India (2003)
important_entities.key_fact: Striking down discriminatory Christian succession laws.
important_entities.significance: The Supreme Court struck down Section 118 of the Indian Succession Act, which imposed unreasonable restrictions on Christians donating property for religious/charitable purposes. Chief Justice V.N. Khare reiterated that a UCC would remove such contradictions and promote national unity.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: If a current affairs question asks: 'The Uttarakhand UCC 2024 applies uniformly to every single citizen residing in the state.' This is **FALSE**. To protect indigenous tribal customs, the Act explicitly exempts **Scheduled Tribes (STs)** from its ambit.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: Live-in Log, No Polygamy, Equal Property, ST Exempt
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Remember the 4 major pillars of the 2024 Uttarakhand UCC: Registration of Live-ins, Monogamy for all, gender parity in inheritance, and tribal exemption.

exam_strategy_tips: In UPSC Mains, when evaluating the Uttarakhand UCC's live-in relationship registry, you must critically analyze it against the Right to Privacy established in **Justice K.S. Puttaswamy (2017)**.
